newsitem.title: ITALY: Fiat European car sales up again in March.
newsitem.headline: Fiat European car sales up again in March.

text.p: Fiat Auto sales in Europe rose 6.8 percent in March year-on-year in a market which fell 3.2 percent overall, giving Fiat a market share of 12.8 percent against 11.6 percent in March 1996, a car sector source said.
The figures confirmed Fiat's second place ranking among European manufacturers behind Germany's Volkswagen.
The Fiat Punto was for the third month running the Turin maker's best selling model with over 60,000 sold in March.
In the first three months of 1997, sales of the Punto totalled 166,000, some 25,000 more than for the VW Golf, the source said.

The Fiat group's Italian market share in March slipped to 43.55 percent from 44.39 percent a year ago, affected by higher than expected demand which could not be fully met by deliveries, the source said.
Of the 2,000 extra workers Fiat recently decided to take on to increase output, just 600 are currently employed while the rest will start work only in the coming months, the source said.
